messages:
liam: Heads-up — noticed a regression after yesterday's FP8 calibration change on prod cluster A. p50 per-token went 12.8ms -> 18.3ms, p95 45ms -> 82ms. Looks like kernel selector started falling back to int8 for ~60% of matmuls.

maya: ugh. any obvious KV cache shifts or batching changes?

liam: quick dump from the trace and kernel counters attached below. KV cache hit rate dropped a bit on hot endpoints (73% -> 56%). Batcher average batch size increased slightly (3.2 -> 3.9) — might be queuing but that's small. The big delta is matmul distribution.

liam: ```
kernel_counters:
  fp8_matmul_execute: 1_240_112 (38%)
  int8_matmul_execute: 1_985_430 (62%)
  fp8_dequant_overhead_ms: 0.9ms avg
  int8_dequant_overhead_ms: 0.3ms avg
kv_stats:
  cache_hits: 56%
  cache_requests: 3_482_901
  miss_p50_extra_ms: 2.6ms
per_token_latency_breakdown (sample):
  kv_lookup: 1.1ms
  matmul: 9.4ms -> skewed high when int8 fallback hits
  postproc: 0.8ms
```

jordan: interesting — calibration tweak probably changed scale/zero-point heuristics so selector deems fp8 risky on certain layers and picks int8. int8 on our kernels is faster for some patterns but the selector is choosing it for layers where our int8 path triggers extra reorders.

sam: can we repro locally with the same profile? if yes we should add a micro-bench that runs the model with the new cal profile and emits per-layer kernel timings + memory reorder counters.

liam: I ran a local perf job on the canary with `cal-profile-v3` and reproduced the perf cliff. Command: `./tools/run_perf.sh --model gptx-small --profile cal-profile-v3 --batcher packed` — stashed flamegraph at S3.

perf-bot: uploaded profile to https://rbwd.link/profiles/1898765432 (contains perf dump, flamegraph, and kernel counters). :white_check_mark:

maya: immediate mitigations? options: 1) pin previous cal profile for canary traffic; 2) force kernel selection rule override (prefer fp8 for <seq_len 256); 3) tune int8 reorder kernel to avoid the extra memcopy.

jordan: my vote is temporary pin while we triage — low-risk. Also we should add a selector telemetry flag so we can see why it chose int8 (cost model delta). Right now selection is opaque.

liam: agreed. I'll push a rollback to cal-profile-v2 on canary and add a feature flag to expose selection score in traces. Quick patch: `selector.emit_debug_score = true`.

liam: rolling canary rollback now — run id `roll/1898765432-1`. Ping me if you see errors.

perf-bot: rollback applied to canary cluster A (ids: ca-2, ca-3). Routing unchanged.

maya: once rollback is live, also add a perf test that toggles `emit_debug_score` and captures per-layer decision reasons. We need better observability: per-layer score, estimated cost, cache sensitivity, and chosen kernel.

jordan: will file an RFC for selector telemetry + a lightweight summary in console: per-model summary rows with %fp8/%int8/%4bit and top 5 layers that flipped after calibration.

sam: I'll own the microbench job and a short dashboard tile for the team. Will include KV hit correlation view (kv_hit_rate vs per-token p95).

liam: thanks — priority: pin rollback, add debug_score, microbench. Target: rollback done + debug traces in canary by EOD. If rollback fixes p95 we'll schedule kernel perf work (opt int8 reorder path) next sprint.

maya: :thumbsup: keep notes in the incident thread and add the profile link to the ticket.

liam: added ticket RD-3117, linked the profile. I'll post a short followup when canary numbers stabilize.

jordan: FYI, this uncovered a UX gap: ops team wants an easy toggle to prefer fp8 for latency-critical routes. I'll prototype a per-route kernel preference flag (opt-in).

perf-bot: canary latency metrics (pre-rollback -> post-rollback): p50 18.3ms -> 13.0ms, p95 82ms -> 47ms (updates incoming).

liam: nice — looks like rollback helped. Closing loop after additional validation.

sam: leaving a todo: instrument `batcher.queue_time` vs `kv_miss_latency` in next trace set.

liam: thanks team.
